note: Re-judged 2026-10-24 (independent auditor, after 66858fa127). RFC 7606 Section 5.3: "When parsing NLRI contained in the attribute, the length of the last NLRI found exceeds the amount of unconsumed data remaining in the attribute." New positive tag on TestRFC7606MPReachNLRIConsistentWithAFISAFIAccepted (moved from RFC8654-3-1): an IPv4 MP_REACH (valid 4-octet next hop) whose last NLRI, 10.0.0.0/8, needs exactly the one remaining octet must give exact ActionNone through ValidateUpdateRFC7606. That is the exact boundary of "exceeds": an off-by-one in ValidateNLRISyntaxAddPath (pos+prefixBytes >= len) turns it red, so it is a genuine conforming input, not merely no-error. Claim and doc comment now match the body. Second positive TestRFC7606MPReachWellFormedAccepted (IPv6 /32 with exactly 4 octets) is also flush. Negative TestRFC7606MPReachNLRIOverrunsAttribute: valid 16-octet IPv6 next hop, /128 with 2 octets, exact SessionReset (the 3(j) consequence) and "overrun". Producer read: validateMPNLRIField -> validateMPNLRISyntax -> ValidateNLRISyntaxAddPath. FINDING (not verdict-changing): the negative's require.Contains("overrun") also matches the next-hop message "... next-hop length N overruns the attribute" and the ADD-PATH "identifier overruns" message; the valid next hop isolates it today, but the assertion would not catch the outcome moving to the next-hop branch. Fix: require.Equal on "RFC 7606 Section 5.3/3(j): NLRI overrun (need 16 bytes, have 2)" and AttrCode 14. Verdict stands.
